title: Operations: pre-drilled holes as entry positions (plunge to full depth instead of helix)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "Another issue is setting pre drilled holes as starting points for some operations so we can dive down and do properly full depth cuts instead of trying to helix down little bit at a time..."

What is missing: a pocket or adaptive operation in closed material always works its own way down (helix or ramp), a little at a time. The usual shop method, drilling a start hole first and plunging the end mill down it to full depth, cannot be set up: the operation does not know a hole is there.

Wanted: on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, Slot and the 3D roughing operations, an "Entry positions (pre-drilled)" group:
- Pick one or more points or existing drilled holes (a drilling operation earlier in the setup, a hole in the model, or a typed point with a diameter and depth).
- At such a position the tool goes straight down the hole at the plunge/rapid-in-clearance feed to the cutting depth and starts the full-depth cut from there, with no helix or ramp. Depth passes may then be full depth (the user's stepdown still rules).
- Regions with no entry position keep the helix or ramp, or are refused if the user chose "pre-drilled only".

Safety (this is a plunge into what the program believes is air):
- The hole must really be there when the operation runs: its source is an earlier operation in the same setup (or carried stock from a previous setup), checked against the stock simulation; a typed point with no drilling behind it is allowed only with the user's explicit "the hole exists" choice, shown in the operation summary and the setup sheet.
- The hole must be at least as wide as the tool plus a clearance and at least as deep as the plunge; otherwise refused by name with the numbers. A hole with a drill-point cone is counted only to its full-diameter depth.
- The entry must lie inside the region to cut, and the first sideways move starts from the hole wall, not from solid.
- The rapid-in-stock and gouge checks stay on: a plunge down a hole that the simulation does not show is refused at the post like any other.

Related: the companion issue on user-set start and exit points (filed with this one); tool kinds for drills are issue 897.

Done means: a closed pocket with a drilled start hole from an earlier operation plunges down the hole and cuts at full depth with no helix (golden CL, simulation clean); a hole too small or too shallow is refused by name in tests; a typed position without a drilling operation is refused unless the explicit choice is set; undo and redo; MCP parameters; the structural UI test covers the group.
